Given the plots of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ above, find ${h}^{′}(1)$ where $h(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}.$
question.worked_solution:
The quotient rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)-f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(1)=\frac{{f}^{′}(1)\cdot g(1)-f(1)\cdot {g}^{′}(1)}{(g(1))^{2}}.
$$

From the graph above, we obtain that $f(1)=0$ and $g(1)=-1.$

Additionally:

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (-5,5)$ equals $\frac{1}{2}.$ So, ${f}^{′}(1)=\frac{1}{2}.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (-1,2)$ equals $-3.$ So, ${g}^{′}(1)=-3$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(1) & =\frac{{f}^{′}(1)\cdot g(1)-f(1)\cdot {g}^{′}(1)}{(g(1))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-1)-0\cdot (-3)}{(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{1}{2})}{1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
